thread_text:
alex_support: FYI Acme reporting repeated 504s on /v1/generate. RequestID=7f4b9a2e, tenant=acme-prod, started ~2026-03-15T02:12Z. They say a simple curl blows latency from 200ms->5s then times out. Can SRE help collect node/pod logs + GPU metrics for repro?

tenant_acme: confirming — we hit it from our side, same RequestID. Happened ~02:12:08 UTC, attached sample curl (we redacted token).

alex_support: paste of the curl they used:
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"rdi-2-large","input":"short prompt"}' \n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

chris_ingest: thx. First things: capture runtime pod logs around requestid, and collect node GPU snapshot. Run (on support-side cluster):
```bash
kubectl -n dedicated-pool logs -l app=redwood-runtime -c runtime --since=10m | grep 7f4b9a2e -n --context=3 > /tmp/repro-runtime.log
kubectl get pods -n dedicated-pool -o wide | grep runtime
# on node where pod landed
ssh node-az2-03 'nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,memory.used,memory.total,utilization.gpu --format=csv' > /tmp/gpu-snapshot.csv
```

maya_sre: also grab dmesg + kubelet logs for node, and a heap of the runtime container for last 1 minute: `kubectl exec -n dedicated-pool <pod> -c runtime -- pmap $(pgrep redwood-runtime) | tail -n 20` (if pmap allowed). If we suspect kernel/XID, grab `dmesg -T | tail -n 200`.

alex_support: copying commands to on-call, starting capture now. Quick question: can we run the debug-bundle tool for this request id or do we need tenant consent?

maya_sre: you can run debug-bundle for a repro requestid — it's covered under support troubleshooting for production issues, but mark it as sensitive and redact tokens. Command we use: `support-debug-bundle collect --request-id 7f4b9a2e --out s3://redwood-support/acme/7f4b9a2e-debug.tgz` — it will pull pod logs, node metrics, and kernel logs.

ops-bot: debug-bundle job started by alex_support for request 7f4b9a2e. JobID=db-20260315-001. Upload will follow to s3 when complete. :gear:

chris_ingest: if you can also run a short sysdig capture to preserve runtime process state while reproducing, that helps. Example (short 10s capture):
```bash
sysdig -w /tmp/repro-7f4b9a2e.scap -p"evt.time %evt.arg" -c echo_fds evt.type=write and container.name contains redwood-runtime & sleep 10
```

alex_support: running debug-bundle + sysdig now. Also grabbed kubelet logs and nvidia-smi. I see one runtime pod restarted around 02:11:59: pod/runtime-7c9f8 crashed then back. Uploading artifacts — presigned link will be posted when done.

maya_sre: quick look at runtime log excerpt (pulled locally):
```
[2026-03-15T02:11:59Z] runtime ERROR request=7f4b9a2e trace=abc123 msg="alloc KV cache failed" details="OOM while allocating 1.2G for kv-cache"
[2026-03-15T02:12:00Z] runtime WARN request=7f4b9a2e msg="falling back to small-batch path"
[2026-03-15T02:12:06Z] runtime ERROR request=7f4b9a2e msg="response timeout"
```

chris_ingest: that suggests GPU memory pressure causing KV allocation failures. From node GPU snapshot: `0, 12245 MiB, 24576 MiB, 98 %` — nearly full. Could be prefix cache buildup. We'll look at batching config and whether this tenant got a burst of long-context requests.

ops-bot: debug-bundle db-20260315-001 completed. Upload URL: https://s3.amazonaws.com/redwood-support/acme/7f4b9a2e-debug.tgz (expires in 72h) :file_folder:

alex_support: uploaded sysdig + extra logs here: https://support-artifacts.internal/acme/7f4b9a2e.tar.gz (internal only). Sharing the s3 presigned with customer ops.

tenant_acme: we can confirm our traffic spiked from an internal batch job at ~02:10:30 which sent 40 concurrent long-context requests. We'll throttle that while you investigate. Thanks for the quick turnaround. :pray:

maya_sre: next steps: SRE to audit prefix/KV cache eviction policy for dedicated cluster, and infra to check autoscale/burst config — if warm KV cache causes allocation failures we'll add guardrails. I'll open a follow-up RFC for cache eviction tweaks. cc @chris_ingest. :thumbsup:

alex_support: closing loop with customer, will follow up with internal findings and upload the RFC link here when available. Thanks team.
